summary.name: Mac Android Subsystem
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS app that runs Android apps on Apple silicon Macs, each in its own window with its own Dock icon and Launchpad entry.
keywords: android on mac without google play
use_cases: Run Android apps on a Mac alongside Mac apps
Sideload APK, APKS or XAPK files on macOS
Play Android games with a console controller on a Mac
Test Android apps through adb and Android Studio on a Mac
Install apps from F-Droid on a Mac
summary.what_it_does: Runs Android inside a lightweight virtual machine that the user does not see, and streams each Android app's display into its own resizable Mac window. Apps get a Dock icon and a Launchpad entry, and Android notifications appear in Notification Centre. APK, APKS and XAPK files can be installed by double-click or drag and drop. Connected Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and MFi controllers are passed to Android as a standard gamepad. Power modes (Smart, Power Saver, Always Ready, As needed) control how much resources Android uses.
notable: Each Android app gets its own Mac window, Dock icon and Launchpad entry
Game controllers work automatically as a standard Android gamepad
Built on LineageOS, QEMU and scrcpy under GPLv3
Developer mode lets adb and Android Studio connect
caveats: No Google Play or Google services; apps needing them may not work
Requires Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later; Intel Macs are not supported
Early release; 3D graphics use software rendering and run slower, multi-touch pinch and rotate are planned
